worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = public pension paid by MT (person 0) 45,000.00 = 45,000.00. Federal taxable income = 45,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 29,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Filing status single, no Montana standard deduction or exemptions. Schedule I Part I: line 7 additions 0.00; line 24 subtractions 0.00. Form 2 page 1: line 1 federal AGI 45,000.00; line 2 Form 1040 lines 12e and 13b 15,750.00; line 3 29,250.00; line 4 0.00; line 5 0.00; line 6 age 65 subtraction 0 x 5,660.00 = 0.00; line 7 Montana taxable income 29,250.00 + 0.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 29,250.00. Page 2 worksheet: line 1 taxable income 29,250.00; no net long-term capital gain, so lines 2-10 are skipped and line 11 is 0.00; line 12 ordinary income tax from the PDF p18 rate table: 5.9% x 29,250.00 = 1,725.75, less 253 = 1,472.75; line 13 = 1,472.75, carried to page 1 line 8. Bracket schedule as numbers (the expected figure): 4.7% x 21,100.00 = 991.70; 5.9% x (29,250.00 - 21,100.00 = 8,150.00) = 480.85; bracket tax 1,472.55. Line 9 nonrefundable credits 0.00; line 10 tax after credits 1,472.55. The form gives 1,472.75; expected keeps the projection's 1,472.55, a difference of 0.20 from the table's whole-dollar constant (253 against 253.20). Montana's own government pension has no subtraction either (settlement fact 2).
accepted_approximations: The tables print a whole-dollar constant with the 5.9% rate (253, 506, 380) where the bracket arithmetic gives 253.20, 506.40, 380.40.
